code_organization.evidence: Improved from 5 to 6. The major improvement is the store decomposition: ConservatoryStore has been split into rootStore.ts (1023 lines, down from 1538), storeState.ts (64 lines), useConservatoryStore.ts (188 lines), queryHooks.ts (46 lines), three repository classes, and ActionCommittalUseCase. The repository pattern is cleanly implemented. TanStack Query is correctly introduced for server-state management. However: (1) DUAL STORE PROBLEM — both rootStore.ts (ConservatoryStore class) and useConservatoryStore.ts (Zustand slice) implement overlapping behavior. App.tsx uses both simultaneously, and PlaygroundScreen imports from both. processVoiceInput exists in both with different implementations. commitAction/commitPendingAction both exist. This duality is a new architectural hazard introduced by this pull. (2) rootStore.ts still uses require() for dynamic imports in initFirestoreSync — a CommonJS pattern in an ESM project. (3) The src/ vs components/ vs utils/ split-root naming issue persists unchanged. (4) BlueprintService.ts and EchoEngine.ts are placeholder stub services with console.log and hardcoded return values committed to main.

Firestore rules still grant broad authenticated read/write on entities, events, groups with no ownership enforcement. NEW FINDING: App.tsx line 41 bypasses authentication entirely with const [user, setUser] = useState<any>({ uid: 'dev-user' }) — the login guard is always satisfied, Firebase Auth is never checked, and LoginView is never shown. This dev shortcut appears to have been committed to main and the existing auth infrastructure in rootStore.ts is now bypassed.
